„Wenn Anträge nicht so funktionieren, wie wir es aus dem privaten Umfeld kennen, verlieren Menschen Vertrauen.“

🌐 How can trusted digital infrastructure and digital identity support collaboration across organizations and borders?

At #GDC2026 in Geneva, UNICC brought its experience to two discussions exploring this question from different perspectives.

UNICC Director Sameer Chauhan joined the panel “Scaling Trust: Sovereign Digital Public Infrastructure for Research, Education, and Innovation in Africa,” co-organized by UNICC, UNESCO, and The World Bank Group. Drawing on the DIGITAfrica project as a concrete example, the discussion explored the technical, governance, and institutional conditions needed to federate research infrastructure and enable trusted recognition of digital credentials across borders.

Pablo A., UNICC Digital ID Solution Architect, also joined the session “Quality Assured Health Wallets: Real-World Use Cases,” sharing UNICC’s experience with reusable identity components, including identity verification, verifiable credentials, offline and paper

2. We zoomed in on infrastructure, standards, co-creation and incentives as foundation to scaling digital interoperable solutions.

27m • 

In July I argued that gatekeeping does not evaporate, it moves up a layer. Today's announcement makes the point concrete: Siri rebuilt on foundation models developed with Google, its most demanding reasoning running on NVIDIA GPUs within Google Cloud, and an assistant that acts inside applications rather than merely opening them.
The question is not product quality, which is likely to be high. It is that the conversational interface becomes the single starting point for user intent, resting on an infrastructural subsoil where Europe holds roughly 5% of global GPU capacity. The DMA already anticipates virtual assistants as core platform services, yet concentration forms faster than regulatory remedies.

Finance is anything but boring.

Neobanks, fintechs, trading platforms and crypto have rewritten how we bank, pay, borrow and invest, right down to the plumbing beneath it all.

Yet, disruption no longer makes a brand matter. Trust, usefulness and a clear reason to choose it do.

Established players need to make their scale useful now. Challengers need to prove they’ll still matter tomorrow. And as finance slips into wallets, shops and platforms, every brand faces the same danger: becoming less visible.

Standing out means knowing your strengths, owning the moments that matter and staying unmistakably you wherever money moves.

I think I just killed the GRC, ISMS, AIMS, Supplier Risk Management Tooling Market!
  
I built a full GRC platform with Claude Code to see if it was actually possible using AI. Here's what I found.

Let's be honest — GRC, ISMS, AI Management, and Supplier Risk processes aren't that complicated. Most teams run them in Excel, which works fine until it doesn't: no collaboration, no audit trail, formulas breaking, and version chaos. So you look at dedicated tooling. But then you find that most point solutions either don't do exactly what you need, cost a significant amount of money, or both. Solution embedded in platforms you already pay for might make more sense (e.g. ServiceNow, Atlassian) but isn't an option for everyone or more difficult to implement.
 
So I built my own. And I built it entirely with Claude Code — partly to see if it was possible, partly to explore how
